note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Patient to telephone the support number in the Babylon app today to arrange a comprehensive blood panel (CBC, renal, liver, thyroid profile, B-12/folate, ferritin, glucose, electrolytes) – requisition form to be generated by clinician.
2. Await blood-test results; patient will receive a text prompt to book a follow-up consultation for review and further management (possible physical examination, medication adjustment, referral).
3. Safety-net advice given: if chest pain, persistent or worsening palpitations, new dyspnoea on exertion, vomiting, or change in bowel habit occurs, attend Emergency Department or contact service urgently.
4. Re-assessment of thyroid status and consideration of restarting levothyroxine to be decided once results available.
5. Low mood and possible depressive symptoms to be re-evaluated at follow-up; consider mental-health referral if symptoms persist after medical causes addressed.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 35-year-old male lawyer presents with 3.5 months of loss of appetite and energy, describing feeling “down” and “out of place.”  
• Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone (~6 kg) over ~6 months.  
• Occasional nausea; no vomiting.  
• Episodic palpitations and sensation of breathlessness mainly in elevators; can walk a mile without dyspnoea but has been largely sedentary recently. No chest pain.  
• Bowels normal; no diarrhoea, blood, or mucus. No reflux.  
• Headaches and decreased libido noted.  
Past Medical History: Primary hypothyroidism.  
Medications: Levothyroxine – stopped several months ago (“dose/route/frequency not documented”). No current regular medications.  
Allergies: Not documented.  
Social: Recently changed law firms (~3.5 months ago); possible work stress. No smoking/alcohol history recorded.

Objective:
• Tele-consultation – no vitals or physical examination performed.  
• No reported exertional dyspnoea or chest pain.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, low mood  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Major depressive disorder (DDx: High likelihood).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Iron-deficiency or other anaemia (Medium); malignancy (lymphoma/GI) (consider but no red-flag GI features); Addison’s disease (Low).  
   - Investigations: CBC, ferritin, B-12/folate, metabolic panel.  
   - Treatment: Pending results; consider mental-health referral/therapy after exclusion of medical causes.

2. Relapsed hypothyroidism (ceased levothyroxine)  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Relapsed / undertreated hypothyroidism (DDx: Medium likelihood).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Hyperthyroidism (variable thyroiditis) (Low).  
   - Investigations: Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4); thyroid antibodies if indicated.  
   - Treatment: Consider resumption/titration of levothyroxine once TFTs reviewed.

3. Episodic palpitations / perceived breathlessness in lifts  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Panic attacks / anxiety disorder (DDx: Medium–Low likelihood).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia or other arrhythmia (consider); sub-acute hyperthyroid state (if TFTs abnormal).  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; consider ECG or Holter monitoring if episodes increase or bloods abnormal.  
   - Treatment: Reassurance today; safety-net advice for chest pain/true dyspnoea; further management after blood results.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Smoking status, alcohol intake, full allergy list, family history, medication reconciliation (other OTC/supplements), mental-health screen (PHQ-9/GAD-7), vitals.  
● Transcript vs DDx conflicts: Weight loss atypical for hypothyroidism (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional interruptions and minor inaudible segments but main clinical content intelligible.
